t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section as a flat straight-on UI mockup on a warm limestone background. Top-left: a large light-weight navy sans headline in sentence case. Top-right: a thin-line navy front elevation drawing of an equipment skid with a vessel, valves, pipe runs and a control panel, no shading, with five small filled steel-blue square tags carrying mono numbers on hairline leaders. Below, a full-width four-column table with hairline row rules and numbered rows matching the tags, mono codes in one column, for <CONTENT>. Square corners, calm.
signature_idea: Numbered steel-blue tags on a skid elevation match the numbered rows of the standards table, so each standard points to a place on the equipment.
strengths: tag-to-row numbering gives the table a real visual idea
steel-blue square tags are a disciplined single accent
mono codes, light headline, hairline rules are on-brand
clean elevation drawing reads as engineering
weaknesses: no navy band; the prompted navy/limestone alternation is missing
drawing shows a metal vessel and gauges, closer to stainless equipment
tag placement is loose; some tags point at nothing specific
table text runs into rules (row 1 and 4 overlap the next rule)
invented clause numbers and limits read as fact
brand_fit_why: Limestone sheet, light headline, mono codes, hairline table and one steel-blue tag colour linking drawing to rows are the brand book closely.
